reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features and pattern-based insights with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both human-intuitive pattern recognition and statistically grounded attribution scores are leveraged to pinpoint features that are present in all misclassified instances and have high model impact despite lacking semantic relevance.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all misclassified instances (e.g., row 13590 and 21096) and check for any feature that appears in every instance despite being semantically unrelated to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all misclassified instances, with emphasis on features that may be spurious (e.g., workclass=Local-gov, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse)

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features (e.g., workclass=Local-gov, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) are likely to be spurious by considering their known semantic relevance to income and whether they correlate with the target class in a non-causal way.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned judgment on whether the shared features are semantically unrelated to income and thus potentially spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, model-agnostic feature importance scores that can reveal which features drive predictions in misclassified instances, especially when combined with intersection-based comparison to identify shared high-impact features. Sensitivity analysis directly measures the impact of removing each feature, helping to isolate spurious dependencies. Together, these tools validate the autonomous observations with quantitative evidence, ensuring that shared features are not only present but also highly influential in misclassification.
